messages:
elaine: Quick favor — can someone run a quick smoke perf+quality pass comparing int8 vs int4 vs fp8 on release/2026-03? Looking for latency (p50/p95), token cost delta, and a small prompt eval (~20 prompts). No full eval, just a sanity sweep to decide whether to enable int4 opt-in. cc @sam @raj

sam: I can run a set on ded-rt tonight. Do you want batch=1 only or also batch=4 for throughput check? And seq_len 512 vs 1024?

elaine: Start with batch=1 and batch=4, seq_len=512. Enable KV caching for the smoke. Keep beams=1. If int4 looks promising we'll extend.

raj: I can do the quick quality sweep. Which prompt set? I have bench/sanity/llm_smoke_20.txt — covers QA, summarization, small reasoning. Use that.

sam: Running int4 now on one shard. Posting raw perf + a short diff of quality. Will ping when bench-bot posts artifacts.

bench-bot: perf artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-artifacts/bench/1799876543/int4_smoke.json :white_check_mark:
- p50: 38ms -> 31ms (int4)
- p95: 202ms -> 165ms
- tokens/slice cost: -42% vs fp8

mike: quick profiler note: int4 run shows a 12% increase in KV copy overhead in the first 3 tokens (cache rehydration). attaching cpu/gpu flame link: https://internal/trace/1799876543/trace.html

raj: Quality quick look: ran the 20 prompts and computed simple exact-match & BLEU where applicable. Int4 vs fp8: exact-match drop ~6%, BLEU mean -4 points. Most regressions are on long-context numeric reasoning prompts (2/20). Int8 is nearly parity with fp8.

jess: That lines up with my local micro-test. Suggest trying int4 + fallback-on-uncertainty (entropy threshold) for token-level fallback to fp8. Also filing a small PR to add a canary rollout rule: if prompt_set_failure > 5% block. PR #3217.

elaine: Good. @sam can you run int8 + fp8 baseline and post a single CSV comparing p50/p95/cost/quality? If int4 quality drop <=5% we can consider canarying to a small tenant. If >5%, keep int4 behind an opt-in flag.

sam: Will do. Command I used for the smoke (so folks can reproduce):
```bash
./scripts/run_smoke_bench --model release/2026-03 \
  --quant=int4 --batch_sizes=1,4 --seq_len=512 \
  --cache=on --prompts=bench/sanity/llm_smoke_20.txt \
  --out=/tmp/int4_smoke.json
```
and same for `--quant=int8` and `--quant=fp8`

mike: Uploaded profiler traces and the aggregated CSV to the ticket: https://redwood/issue/ENG-4290. CSV columns: quant, batch, p50_ms, p95_ms, token_cost_usd, exact_match_pct, notes.

raj: One more datapoint: int4 produced a few hallucinations on the summarization prompts (small fabrications). Might be model sensitivity, not just quantization. I'll run a small constrained decoding run to verify.

jess: If we go canary, recommend route config: 5% traffic to int4 in dedicated pool + automatic rollback if quality regression >5% over rolling 1h. I added a draft rollout snippet in PR #3217.

elaine: Thanks all. Action items: sam — post int8+fp8 CSV and upload artifacts to ENG-4290; raj — follow-up constrained-decode checks; jess — finalize canary config PR; mike — keep profiler links in ticket. I'll decide on canary after reviewing CSV. :thumbsup:

sam: Uploaded CSV and artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/bench/1799876543/summary.csv :eyes:

bench-bot: summary.csv checksum: ff12a4b3

mike: quick note — for future runs let's add `--quant-dequant-scheme=adaptive` flag for int4 experiments to see if that narrows quality gap. small change in runtime.

elaine: Good suggestion. If adaptive reduces drop to <=3% we flip to canary. Otherwise keep opt-in. Thanks everyone.

sam: ack, will queue an adaptive run tomorrow morning.

raj: looping in the release notes: adding a short paragraph about int4 experimental status and opt-in flag.

jess: :rocket:

elaine: Closing the thread for now — follow-ups in ENG-4290.
